A1.justification: Both 19-page PDFs describe the same PERMU study. Text, equations, figures, tables and end matter support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original unlearning experiments, layer-level diagnostics, generation-quality evaluations and ablations in Sections 4, 6 and 7.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds ECO comparison results in Tables 3 and 4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains MSM-based token selection, embedding perturbation, distribution subtraction and distribution-matching training. The fast subject-token variant and discrete-token perturbation variant already appear in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TOFU, Harry Potter, ZsRE, WMDP BIO and MUSE BOOK, including the same rephrasing, subject-replacement, reversed-relation and one-hop scenarios. Removing the UGBench name does not remove its underlying evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: ECO-Zero-Out is added to the TOFU comparisons in Tables 3 and 4. Although Section 3.3 changes its count from 13 to 15 algorithms and adds an RMU description, RMU was already evaluated in v2 Tables 11 and 12.

E3.justification: The newly added ECO evaluation uses released TOFU scope-classifier checkpoints and selects Zero-Out to control utility and generation-quality differences. Existing experiments retain their splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets and PERMU hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The layer analyses, paraphrased-answer diagnostics, fluency evaluation, case studies and PERMU ablations are retained. The retain-loss, tuning-coefficient and discrete-token studies are reordered and renumbered, with unchanged experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Section 3.4 states that results are averaged over three runs in both versions. Run counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Pre-existing numerical table content matches after accounting for relocation. New ECO entries alter comparisons: Table 3 reports ECO Forget Probability 17.45 and FRT 2.43 versus unchanged PERMU values 39.02 and 1.72. In Table 4, rephrased Forget05 Probability is 36.87 for ECO versus 31.63 for PERMU.

T1.justification: The problem definition, MSM matrix, Proposition 5.1 and PERMU objective remain unchanged, with no new proof or revised assumptions. The added generic weighted RMU loss explains an existing baseline rather than introducing new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: V3 drops the claim of introducing UGBench as the first comprehensive benchmark and presents that contribution as an evaluation of 15 methods. The generalisation diagnosis, PERMU contribution and headline 50.40% and 40.73% performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explicit comparability argument distinguishing RMU's hazardous-distribution objective from full-forget-set unlearning, and explains ECO variant selection through fluency tradeoffs. Its separate Limitations section emphasizes token-gradient costs at scale; human-evaluation plans and reasoning-related difficulties were already discussed in v2.

D1.justification: V3 documents ECO checkpoint use and variant selection, and expands RMU's technical description. The advertised code repository changes from UGBench to PERMU. Previously reported hardware, training settings and PERMU implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning narrows from a novel named benchmark to a comprehensive evaluation, and v3 explicitly distinguishes its setting from RMU's objective. The cited works are unchanged; ECO's reference receives a publication-metadata update rather than becoming a new citation.

P1.justification: V3 selectively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method motivation and conclusion, retitles Sections 3, 4 and 6, reorders three ablation subsections and introduces a separate Limitations heading. Most exposition and the overall document structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Tables 3 and 4 gain ECO rows, and case-study color emphasis changes. Figures and tables are repositioned, including the renumbered ablation tables. The other research plots retain their visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Adding ECO and clarifying comparison limits improve completeness and transparency. However, v3 retains v2's Table 3 superiority narrative despite ECO now reporting better Forget Probability and FRT than PERMU; Table 4 also retains margins based on earlier comparators without discussing ECO. The useful additional evidence and clearer qualifications coexist with an unreconciled central performance narrative, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
